Q1. Which of the following are true statements:
1. (A) If the known value is 5.2 and the measurements taken are 4.1, 4, 3.8, 4.2, this would be relatively low precision but high accuracy.
2. (B) Accuracy is also known as Precision.
3. (C) If the known value is 9.8 and the measurements taken are 9.8, 9.7, 9.75, 9.85, this would be relatively high precision and high accuracy.
4. (D) If the known value is 15 and the measurements taken are 5.8, 7.9, 11.5, 17.8, this would be relatively low precision and low accuracy.
meas
  • A) C, D
  • B) A, C
  • C) A, C, D
  • D) A, B, D
Accuracy is how close the measured values are to the known value. Precision is how close the measured values are to each other regardless of the accuracy to the known value.

Answer: A
Q2. A declining curve on a mass diagram indicates
constr
  • A) excavation
  • B) embankment
  • C) lower elevation
  • D) cut
A falling mass diagram curve indicates material is being used as fill.

Answer: B
Q3. In order to set curb stakes for 1 mile of new curbs, a precision of 0.01 feet is needed. What would be the most efficient method for setting the stakes given the precision requirements?
meas
  • A) RTK GPS
  • B) Static GPS
  • C) Photogrammetry
  • D) Total station
Static GPS may work however it is not practical for a 1 mile project as when used by itself would be incredibly time consuming. RTK GPS will of course have worse precision than Static and has precision of 2-3 cm. Photogrammetry has even worse accuracy. Total station is the only one that will work here that combines accuracy with efficiency.

Answer: D
Q4. What is the minimum number of control points (horizontal and vertical) needed for a survey of a roadway project?
hc
  • A) 1V, 4H
  • B) 2V, 2H
  • C) 2V, 3H
  • D) 3V, 2H
A minimum of 3 horizontal control points are needed. More is better. If GNSS RTK is used, 4 is needed. The horizontal control should be spread apart, ideally at least 1 in each quadrant of the project. A minimum of 2 vertical control points are needed and should be on opposite ends of the project. Again more is better.

Answer: C
Q5. A pipeline is to be installed between Point E and Point F. A point of interest has been spotted at Point G. What is the station and offset of Point G?
hc
  • A) STA 4+76.98, Offset 164.55' West
  • B) STA 4+53.27, Offset 142.21' West
  • C) STA 5+43.12, Offset 187.93' East
  • D) STA 5+38.83, Offset 249.81' West
Remember that a station is only along a defined linear line. Points adjacent to this line (such point G) are defined as offsets. So the station at G is the same as the point of intersection between line EF and a line from G perpendicular to line EF. The distance from this point of intersection to point G is the offset distance (line HG). Bearing of line EF: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{departure}{latitude} = \dfrac{672.34-289.17}{72.87-417.83} = -1.11077\) \(\theta = -48.0039\) \(bearing\ EF = S48.0039^\circ E = S48^\circ0'14"E\) Bearing of line EG: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{departure}{latitude} = \dfrac{318.76-289.17}{169.78-417.83} = -0.117113\) \(\theta = -6.8027\) \(bearing\ EG = S6.8027^\circ E = S6^\circ48'10"E\) Angle E: \(Angle\ E = 48.003949 - 6.8027 = 41.2013^\circ\) Distance EG: \(EH = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}\) \(EG = \sqrt{(318.76-289.17)^2+(169.78-417.83)^2}\) \(EG = 249.809'\) Use the right triangle to find Distance EH and HG: \(Distance\ EH = \cos(41.2013)(249.809) = 187.96'\) \(Distance\ HG = \sin(41.2013)(249.809) = 164.55'\) Find Station of G (Station H = Station G): \(289.02+187.96 = 476.98'\) \(Station\ at\ G = 4+76.98\) Distance HG = offset from pipe: \(HG = 164.55\ ft = offset\ west\ from\ pipe\)
Note: Of course, only solve for what you need. As you can see, the answers are all different so once you find either the station or the offset, that is all you need to pick an answer. Also, a problem like this is one of the main reasons that a TI-89 is useful. Since calculations are saved in the memory automatically, they can be recalled easily.

Answer: A
Q6. In a photograph taken for an aerial survey, the flight height above the mean sea level is 1780 ft. The height above the sea level is 300 ft. If the focal length is 152.4 mm, what is most nearly the scale of the photo?
photo
  • A) 1 in/300 ft
  • B) 1:250
  • C) 1/3000
  • D) 1 in/17 ft
\(152.4\ mm = 6\ in\) \(Photo\ scale = \dfrac{f}{H-h}\) \(= \dfrac{6\ in}{1780\ ft-300\ ft} = \dfrac{6\ in}{1480\ ft} = \dfrac{1\ in}{246.7\ ft} \approx \dfrac{1\ in}{250\ ft} = \dfrac{1}{3000}\)

Answer: C
Q7. Two curves are formed to create a reverse curve. Both simple curves have the same degree of curvature. What is the station of the PRC?
hc
  • A) 34+77.70
  • B) 41+11.68
  • C) 36+73.14
  • D) 43+66.03
Example As shown in the example stationing above, stationing along the curve and along the curve are seperate and different. When laying out a curve there can actually be 2 stationings, one along the tangent and one along the curve. The first would be the stationing along the tangent. This would allow for laying out the curve. Then once the curve is set, the tangent stationing is discarded and we only now use the curve stationing. This two sets of stationing only comes to play when there is stationing along the tangent that meets the PI. Degree of curvature is the same for both curves therefore their radius is the same. \(T_{total} = R\tan\dfrac{I}{2}\) \(2000 = R\tan\dfrac{60^\circ}{2} + R\tan\dfrac{30^\circ}{2}\) \(2000 = R(\tan30^\circ+\tan15^\circ)\) \(R = 2366.025'\) \(T_1 = R\tan\dfrac{I}{2}\) \(T_1 = 2366.025(\tan30^\circ) = 1366.025'\) \(station\ @\ PC = (5+00)+(25+00)-(13+66.025) = 16+33.98\) \(L_1 = \dfrac{2\pi RI}{360} = \dfrac{2\pi(2366.025)(60)}{360} = 2477.696'\) \(station\ @\ PRC = (16+33.98)+(24+77.696) = 41+11.68\)

Answer: B

Q9. A 50' easement is to be acquired by a city for utility purposes from a square lot. The area of this easement within the lot is
area
  • A) 0.784 acres
  • B) 0.801 acres
  • C) 0.771 acres
  • D) 0.762 acres
\(N39^\circ41'41"E - N1^\circ13'49"E = 38^\circ27'52"\) \(\dfrac{50}{x_1} = \tan(38^\circ27'52")\) \(x_1 = 62.94\ ft\) \(180^\circ-88^\circ46'11"-39^\circ41'41" = 51^\circ32'8"\) \(\dfrac{50}{x_2} = \tan(51^\circ32'8")\) \(x_2 = 39.72\ ft\) \(723.13-62.94-39.72 = 620.47\ ft\) \(620.47\times50 + \left(\dfrac{62.94(50)}{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{39.72(50)}{2}\right) = 33590\ ft^2\) \(\dfrac{33590\ ft^2}{43560\ ft^2/acres} = 0.771\ acres\)

Answer: C

Q10. The bottom of a structure's overhang is known to have an elevation of 220.50. In recent years, the structure has settled. What is the difference in elevation between the original elevation of the bottom of the overhang and the current elevation?
level
  • A) 0.25 ft
  • B) 0.27 ft
  • C) 0.21 ft
  • D) 0.24 ft
The last rod which is usually a fore sight that is subtracted will be added. An inverted rod means that the rod is flipped upside down for occasions like in this problem. \(210.00 + 3.32 - 4.15 + 2.89 - 4.82 + 1.51 + 11.54 = 220.29\) Elevation difference between original and current: \(220.50 - 220.29 = 0.21\ ft\)

Answer: C
Q11. An offset stake is shown with information missing and cut off. A level is set up on the bench. What is the "X" value of the side slopes for the ditch?
constr
  • A) 2.5
  • B) 4
  • C) 3.5
  • D) 3
We must use the stake information and the leveling information to find the side slope ratio for the ditch. The height of the instrument (HI) is 5.3' because we know that the side slopes of the ditch are the same. \(Height\ of\ ditch = 8.2-5.3\) \(Height\ of\ ditch = 2.9\) To find the width of the side slopes, we must calculate the total length and subtract the known values. \(47.50-5-7.8-5-12.3 = 17.4\) \(length\ of\ each\ side\ slope = \dfrac{17.4}{2} = 8.7\) \(Grade = \dfrac{8.7}{2.9} = 3\)

Answer: D
Q12. A map has a scale of 1 in:400 ft. A square building area measures 0.09 square inches. The ground area of the building is
area
  • A) 3888 sq ft
  • B) 14400 sq ft
  • C) 1296 sq ft
  • D) 10280 sq ft
\(1\ in : 400\ ft\) \(1\ in^2 : 160000\ ft^2\) \(0.09\times160000 = 14400\) \(\downarrow\) \(0.09\ in^2 : 14400\ ft^2\)

Answer: B
Q13. A highway is to be constructed where the road must provide a clearance of 3 ft from the top of a sewer line (ID=12", OD=16") The grade from PVI to EVC is
vc
  • A) 1.18%
  • B) 1.06%
  • C) 0.22%
  • D) 2.17%
\(BVC = 13+97-5+00 = 8+97\) \(elev_{BVC} = elev_V + G_1(\dfrac{L}{2})\) \(elev_{BVC} = 16.03+2.94(5) = 30.73\) \(elev_{14+23} = 16.63+1'ID+\left(\dfrac{2}{12}\right)'OD+3'cover\) \(elev_{14+23} = 20.80\ ft\) \(elev_x = \dfrac{Rx^2}{2}+g_1x+elev_{BVC}\) \(x = 1423-897 = 526\ ft = 5+26\) \(20.80 = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{g_2+2.94}{10}\right)5.26^2}{2}-2.94(5.26)+30.73\) \(g_2 = 1.06\%\)
Note: If this point was known to be the low point, we could have used the Do equation and simply solve for the missing grade after find the distance to station 14+23. But that is not know and in fact will give you the wrong answer.

Answer: B

Q15. A circular trench that is 3.5 ft deep will be dug in the shaded area. The total excavated volume is
area
  • A) 43015 yd³
  • B) 27124 yd³
  • C) 10754 yd³
  • D) 12290 yd³
\(R_2^2-R_1^2 = 325^2\) \(shaded\ area\ volume = (\pi R_2^2-\pi R_1^2)(3.5)\) \(shaded\ area\ volume = \pi(R_2^2-R_1^2)(3.5)\) \(shaded\ area\ volume = \pi(325^2)(3.5)\) \(shaded\ area\ volume = 1161407.53\ ft^3\) \(\dfrac{1161407.53\ ft^3}{27\ ft^3/yd^3} = 43015\ yd^3\)

Answer: A
Q16. Line AC= 310.28 ft. Distance AB is
hc
  • A) 137.73'
  • B) 188.91'
  • C) 154.46'
  • D) 121.37'
\(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)\) \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1056.04-901.58}{958.22-937.40}\right)\) \(Bearing\ CD = 82^\circ19'24" = N82^\circ19'24"E\) \(Distance\ CD = \sqrt{(1056.04-901.58)^2+(958.22-937.40)^2}\) \(Distance\ CD = 155.86\ ft\) \(\angle BCD = N21^\circ59'1"W + N82^\circ19'24"E\) \(\angle BCD = 104^\circ18'25"\) Law of Sine: \(\dfrac{\sin104^\circ18'25"}{273} = \dfrac{\sin\angle CBD}{155.86}\) \(\angle CBD = 33^\circ35'15"\) \(\angle CDB = 180^\circ-104^\circ18'25"-33^\circ35'15"\) \(\angle CDB = 42^\circ6'20"\) \(\dfrac{\sin104^\circ18'25"}{273} = \dfrac{\sin42^\circ6'20"}{BC}\) \(BC = 188.91\ ft\) \(AB = 310.28-188.91 = 121.37\ ft\)

Answer: D
Q17. Which of the following is the most efficient and preferred method for creating a topographic map?
topo
  • A) Stadia method
  • B) Three-wire method
  • C) Radiation method
  • D) Offset method
Radiation method means that an instrument is set up on a benchmark that can be seen by most or all points by turning the instrument radially around the z-axis. This limits the number of setups needed which will be the most efficient and accurate way of surveying for a topo. The other options are either not used for a topo, are far too slow, or not accurate. Stadia method uses uses the stadia hairs which are viewed through a level to find distance and elevations. This method is not efficient and many times too inaccurate. Offset method is not a real method used for topographic maps. Three-wire method uses all three stadia hairs and averages them to find the correct reading. This method is far too slow for most uses especially for a topo. Also note that if you do not recognize a word or do not know its definition, you can look it up in the glossary in the manual.

Answer: C
Q18. In laying out a highway for construction, a cut beginning at sta 11+78.45 is necessary until the existing ground elevation matches the proposed elevation. The proposed elevation is 356.42 ft. The existing ground elevation at sta 11+78.45 is 371.13 ft. If the 3:1 cut slope is to be implemented along the centerline, the station at the catchpoint is
constr
  • A) 11+83.35
  • B) 11+73.55
  • C) 11+93.16
  • D) 12+22.58
\(371.13-356.42 = 14.71\ ft\ elevation\ change\) \(\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{14.71}{x}\) \(x = 44.13\ ft\) \(11+78.45+0+44.13 = 12+22.58\) Remember 3:1 slope in the english system (in, ft) is horizontal:vertical for surveying. Also remember that catchpoint is where elevations meet.

Answer: D
Q19. What is the most precise method of finding vertical points?
level
  • A) differential leveling
  • B) three-wire leveling
  • C) indirect leveling
  • D) double-rodded leveling
Three-wire leveling is the most accurate as it averages the three lines through the scope instead of just using the middle cross hair. Differential leveling is a general term. Indirect leveling uses angles to find vertical and horizontal distance. All can be found in the glossary.

Answer: B

\(121^\circ42'34"-90^\circ = 31^\circ42'34"\) \(\tan31^\circ42'34" = \dfrac{x}{164.24}\) \(x = 101.47\ ft\) \(101.47+214.13 = 315.60\ ft\)

Q21. BM1 is 1.23 miles from BM2. What is the maximum second order class II vertical error for this run?
level
  • A) 1.829 ft
  • B) 0.072 ft
  • C) 0.006 ft
  • D) 0.0047 ft
\(max\ error = 1.3mm\sqrt{K}\) \(1.23\ mile = 1.979\ km\) \(max\ error = 1.3\sqrt{1.979} = 1.829\ mm = 0.072\ in = 0.006\ ft\)

Answer: C
Q22. The approximate area under the curve in square feet is
area
  • A) 6166 sq ft
  • B) 5157 sq ft
  • C) 1720 sq ft
  • D) 15473 sq ft
Convert station interval to yards: \(\dfrac{20\ ft}{3} = 6.666\ yds\) Find area using the equation for constant station interval: \(Area = a\left(\dfrac{h_0}{2}+h_1+h_2+h_3+h_4+\dfrac{h_5}{2}\right)\) \(Area = 6.666\left(\dfrac{13.46}{2}+18.89+17.78+14.51+17.97+\dfrac{20.16}{2}\right)\) \(Area = 573\ yd^2\) \(573\ yd^2\times\dfrac{9\ ft^2}{1\ yd^2} = 5157\ ft^2\)
Note: This method will not give us the exact answer. It will give us an an approximate area under the curve which is very close to the exact anwer. Using any other method would take too long and is really outside the scope of the exam. On the real exam, if you run into a problem like this, just use the equation.

Answer: B
Q23. What is the interior angle measurement at point E?
trav
  • A) 266°37'55"
  • B) 91°3'22"
  • C) 93°22'3"
  • D) 274°12'57"
The simpliest way to answer this question is to find the last exterior angle and subtract that from 360 degrees. \(all\ exterior\ angles = 180^\circ(n+2)\) \(all\ exterior\ angles = 180^\circ(5+2)\) \(all\ exterior\ angles = 1260^\circ\) Exterior angle at E: \(1260^\circ-250^\circ34'54"-221^\circ19'16"-270^\circ19'31"-251^\circ8'22"\) \(exterior\ angle\ at\ E = 266^\circ37'55"\) Interior angle at E: \(360^\circ-266^\circ37'55" = 93^\circ22'3"\)
Note: The solution diagram's angle label at E reads 266°37'57", which differs by 2" from the computed value of 266°37'55" used in the worked steps above (and which correctly yields the marked answer, 93°22'3"). The computed value has been confirmed correct by the instructor; the 2" difference is a minor labeling artifact in the source diagram.

Answer: C
Q24. The bearing and azimuth of DE is
hc
  • A) DE = S 75°7'55" E, azimuth = 165°7'55"
  • B) DE = S 66°20'44" E, azimuth = 156°22'44"
  • C) DE = S 75°7'55" E, azimuth = 104°52'5"
  • D) DE = S 66°20'44" E, azimuth = 113°39'16"
\(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right) = 9^\circ27'44"\) \(90^\circ-9^\circ27'44"-62^\circ17'21" = 18^\circ14'55"\) \(18^\circ14'55"+62^\circ17'21" = 80^\circ32'16"\) \(azimuth\ BD = 80^\circ32'16"\) \(80^\circ32'16"+33^\circ7' = 113^\circ39'16"\) \(180^\circ-113^\circ39'16" = 66^\circ20'44"\) \(bearing\ DE = S66^\circ20'44"E\) \(azimuth = 180^\circ-66^\circ20'44" = 113^\circ39'16"\)

Answer: D
Q25. A survey crew has placed an instrument 250 ft horizontally from the center of the base of an antenna tower with a rod reading of 5.84 ft. The instrument is also 350 feet from Benchmark A at elevation 138.64 feet. A vertical angle of 13.6 is measured to the top of the tower. What is most nearly the height of the antenna tower?
ang
  • A) 61.17 ft
  • B) 66.32 ft
  • C) 59.13 ft
  • D) 66.95 ft
The benchmark information is extra and not needed for this question. Given the vertical angle from the instrument sight and distance to the tower, solve for the height from the instrument sight and add the rod reading to obtain the height of the tower. \(H_{tower} = H\times\tan(\alpha)+RR\) \(H_{tower} = 250.0ft\times\tan(13.6^\circ)+5.84ft\) \(H_{tower} = 66.32\ ft\)

Answer: B
Q26. The new Terrace View Apartment building will be ten equally sized floors when completed. The first three floors have been built and the fourth floor is currently under construction. The FS survey rod was located at the face of the building. How tall is the building to the top of the completed second floor?
ang
  • A) 24.00 ft
  • B) 12.00 ft
  • C) 20.75 ft
  • D) 36.00 ft
Considering that all the floors are equally sized, we can find the height of the 3rd floor, then divide by 3 to find the height of each floor, then multiple by 2 for the height of the second floor. Height of third floor: \(Height_{3rdFloor} = FS+H\tan(24^\circ)\) \(Height_{3rdFloor} = 8.75ft+61.20ft\times\tan(24^\circ)\) \(Height_{3rdFloor} = 36.00\ ft\) Height of second floor: \(Height_{EachFloor} = \dfrac{36}{3} = 12\ feet\) \(Height_{2ndFloor} = 12\ feet\times2\ floors = 24\ feet\)
Note: It may be hard to figure out what distance the "H" value is measuring in the image however typically the variable is centered between the distance or ends when there is a clear end point like the start of a curve or, in this case, between an instrument and a building.

Answer: A
Q27. The sum of the interior angles of a 6-sided closed traverse with a 23 second angular misclosure can be
trav
  • A) 360°00'23"
  • B) 1079°59'37"
  • C) 359°59'37"
  • D) 719°59'37"
\((n-2)(180) = 4(180) = 720\) \(720^\circ\pm0^\circ00'23" = 719^\circ59'37"\ or\ 720^\circ00'23"\)

Answer: D
Q28. What is used to convert between the horizontal datums NAD 27 and NAD 83?
theory
  • A) 12 cm shift
  • B) NADCON
  • C) VERTCON
  • D) 18 cm shift
The shift between the various datums are not uniform across the United States and there is no single value that can be applied to latitudes or to longitudes based on old datums to convert them to NAD 83. NADCON was developed in order to facilitate conversion between the datums. The grids used by the program are based on more than 150,000 horizontal control points whose coordinates reside in NGS' data base, and provide transformed positions based on the shifts of the control nearest to the input position.

Answer: B
Q29. For the two reverse curves below, what is the length of CD?
hc
  • A) 723.37'
  • B) 205.23'
  • C) 415.12'
  • D) 518.37'
The angle created where the tangent of the curve and the radius meet always creates a 90 degree angle. \(Angle\ D = 180-90-57\) \(Angle\ D = 33^\circ\) Law of sine: \(\dfrac{\sin A}{a} = \dfrac{\sin D}{d}\) \(\dfrac{\sin90^\circ}{a} = \dfrac{\sin33^\circ}{620}\) \(a = 1138.37\) \(line\ CD = 1138.37-620 = 518.37'\)

Answer: D

Q31. Determine the approximate volume of concrete needed to construct the channel between station 5+00 and 20+00.
constr
StationsHeight (H)
5+002.5ft
20+002.5ft
  • A) 240 cy
  • B) 230 cy
  • C) 225 cy
  • D) 285 cy
Triangle with X1 (parallelogram): \(Side\ slope = \tan^{-1}(1/2) = 26.565\) \(X_1 = \dfrac{4}{\sin26.565} = 8.94in\) Triangle with X2 (trapezoid): \(X_2 = \dfrac{4}{\tan26.565} = 8.00in\) Area 1 and 3 are identical parallelograms. Note: The area of a parallelogram is base times height. The height does not have to be within the parallelogram. It just has to span from the base to the top. Therefore the height for these parallelograms is 2.5 feet. \(Areas\ 1\ and\ 3 = 2\left(2.5\times\dfrac{8.94}{12}\right) = 3.73\ ft^2\) Area 2 (ABCD): \(CD = 5-2(8.94\div12) = 3.51ft\) \(AB = 3.51+\left(\dfrac{8.00+8.00}{12}\right) = 4.84ft\) \(Area = \left(\dfrac{3.51+4.84}{2}\right)\dfrac{4}{12} = 1.39ft^2\) Total Volume: \(Volume = Area\times Length\) \(Volume = (2000-500)\times(1.39+3.73)\dfrac{1cy}{27ft^3}\) \(Volume = 284.4\ cy\)

Answer: D
Q32. Which of the following is an example of spatial data?
gis
  • A) Event schedule at outdoor theater
  • B) All of these
  • C) Weather patterns on a particular day
  • D) Parcels showing land use and area
Spatial data is a term used to describe any data related to or containing information about a specific location on the Earth's surface. Therefore there is only one answer choice that fits.

Answer: D
Q33. A proposed sewer line extension is shown in the profile. The drafter mistakenly used 6" HDPE pipe instead of the specified 8" HDPE pipe. This means that the connection of the invert in the existing manhole will result in a top of pipe elevation too high to satisfy the 3 foot cover requirement. If the slope of the new pipe is lowered to 0.2%, what is the vertical exaggeration?
constr
  • A) 0.13
  • B) 0.1
  • C) 7.5
  • D) 3.0
Regardless of what is happening in the problem, the vertical exaggeration is the vertical scale divided by the horizontal scale of a profile \(Vertical\ exaggeration = \dfrac{V_{scale}}{H_{scale}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1"}{4'}}{\dfrac{1"}{30'}} = \dfrac{30}{4} = 7.5\)

Answer: C
Q34. The City of Bakersfield has approved the construction of a new development on Stockdale Hwy. As part of the development, utilities will need to be connected to existing utilities along the roadway. As-builts were found from 1998 and show that the water line is about 6.5 feet from grade. However, the as-built plans also show that there may be some shallow utilities. What is the best way to locate the exact location of the waterline?
constr
  • A) using original designs plans
  • B) exploratory excavation (pot-holing)
  • C) calling the utility provider
  • D) using as-built plans
The only way to know exactly where the waterline is located is to physically measure it. Therefore a small hole must be dug leading straight to the top of the waterline so that it can be directly measured. As-builts would be the second option as they are supposed to contain records of the final location of all fixed works but should only be used for planning purposes.

Answer: B
Q35. A 700 ft sag curve has a -3% grade and a 5% grade. If the center of the curve was raised 3 ft while the respective grades stayed the same, the new length of the curve would be
vc
  • A) 700 ft
  • B) 1000 ft
  • C) 900 ft
  • D) 800 ft
\(m = \dfrac{(G'-G)L}{8}\) \(m = \dfrac{(5+3)7}{8}\) \(m = 7\ ft\) \(7\ ft+3\ ft = 10 = m'\) \(m' = \dfrac{(G'-G)L'}{8}\) \(10 = \dfrac{(5+3)L'}{8}\) \(L' = 10\ sta = 1000\ ft\)

Answer: B
Q36. What is the best way to locate high-risk underground utilities?
constr
  • A) existing roadway plans
  • B) existing utility plans
  • C) perform pot-holing
  • D) existing as-built plans
While as-built plans, utility plans, and roadway plans should all show underground utilities, it may not be exactly where they say it should be. In order to verify their exact location, a pot-hole survey should be conducted. This would include cutting a small circular hole of the roadway and digging down (usually using a suction vacuum) to the utility to verify exactly where it is. This would ensure that the underground utilities will not be harmed by new construction.

Answer: C
Q37. What is the length of the direct line AF?
trav
  • A) 167.93'
  • B) 167.64'
  • C) 136.62'
  • D) 136.86'
Calculate the change in x and y (departure and latitude) then use those values to find the length from point A to point F. \(\triangle X_{ABCDEF} = 37.0+20.5+48.2+30.9 = 136.6\) \(\triangle Y_{ABCDEF} = 21.3-12.7+23.1-11.7-28.4 = -8.4\) \(Length = \sqrt{(\triangle X)^2+(\triangle Y)^2}\) \(Length\ AF = \sqrt{(136.6)^2+(-8.4)^2}\) \(Length\ AF = 136.86\ feet\)
Note: Another way to do it is to use the coordinates of point A and point F to find the length but that would take longer.

Answer: D

pls

hc

\(1289.20-1150.70 = 138.50\) \(1180.90-1125.30 = 55.60\) \(\sqrt{138.50^2+55.60^2} = 149.24\ ft\) \(L_{curve\ 1} = \dfrac{2\pi RI}{360^\circ} = \dfrac{2(\pi)(450)(39^\circ0'3")}{360}\) \(L_{curve\ 1} = 306.31\ ft\) \(L_{curve\ 2} = \dfrac{2\pi RI}{360^\circ} = \dfrac{2(\pi)(370)(54^\circ51'7")}{360}\) \(L_{curve\ 2} = 354.22\ ft\) \(200\ ft+306.31\ ft+149.24\ ft+354.22\ ft+75\ ft = 1085\ ft\) \(2750+1085 = 3835 = 38+35\)

Q43. Which among the following is/are true regarding LiDAR?
1. LiDAR is a surveying method that measures distance of a target by illuminating that target with a pulsed laser light, and measuring the reflected pulses with a sensor.
2. It is the most accurate data transmission technique in which light is used as medium.
lidar
  • A) 1 only
  • B) Neither 1 nor 2
  • C) 2 only
  • D) Both 1 and 2
LiDAR stands for Light Detection and Ranging, is a remote sensing method that uses light in the form of a pulsed laser to measure ranges (variable distances) to the Earth. These light pulses — combined with other data recorded by the airborne system — generate precise, three dimensional information about the shape of the Earth and its surface characteristics. LiDAR is a remote sensing technology that measures distance by illuminating a target with a laser and analyzing the reflected light. A LiDAR instrument principally consists of a laser, a scanner, and a specialized GPS receiver. LiDAR is highly accurate scientific surface/topographic data with active sensing system and it uses its own energy source, not reflecting naturally or naturally emitted radiation. This mode allows direct acquisition of terrain information.

Q44. A measurement of 4800 feet was taken from point B to point C. If the relative accuracy of the measurement is 1:20,000, what is the maximum error?
meas

Answer: D
Q45. A new building storm drain line is being connected to the 84" storm drain mainline in the street. After evaluating the area, it was determined that the shortest path from the building to the mainline will be used. What is the azimuth of this storm drain lateral from the mainline?
hc
  • A) 269°57'29"
  • B) 229°54'16"
  • C) 222°3'30"
  • D) 220°5'44"
In order for the storm drain lateral distance to be as short as possible, the lateral must be perpendicular to the mainline (also know as the offset distance which is the distance parallel to the mainline). Therefore the azimuth of the lateral should be 90 degrees to the bearing of the mainline. Bearing of storm drain mainline: \(Bearing\ of\ storm\ drain\ mainline = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{-193.90-214.19}{1140.01-655.31}\right) = -40.0955^\circ\) \(Bearing\ of\ storm\ drain\ mainline\ MH2\ to\ MH3 = S40^\circ5'44"E\) \(Azimuth\ of\ the\ shortest\ path = 90^\circ+(90^\circ-40^\circ5'44")+90^\circ = 229^\circ54'16"\)
Note: The "W" next to the x value means that the coordiante is left of the zero point. You can think of it as a negative value. For example MH2 in (x,y) would be (-193.90, 1140.01). MH3 in (x,y) would be (214.19, 655.31)

Answer: B
Q46. What is the best instrument to use to perform a topographic survey of a forest area with lots of dense trees?
topo
  • A) GPS
  • B) Total Station
  • C) Transit Level
  • D) Theodolite
Topographic surveys show all necessary information to design a project such as elevations and distances. Considering a theodolite and transit are similar, these can be crossed out immediately as there is only 1 correct answer. But the reason they don't work best is because these instruments are slow to use and are inaccurate for distance (by use of stadia). GPS is great for a topographic survey however without a clear view of the sky, it is useless for this project. Therefore a total station is the best instrument to use here as it does not require clear skies and can measure distance (by use of EDM).

Answer: B
Q47. On a plan and profile sheet, the vertical scale of a proposed pipeline is 1/60. The ground horizontal distance between MH1 and MH2 is 79.4'. The vertical exaggeration is 6:1. What is this horizontal distance on the plan and profile sheet?
photo
  • A) 13.23"
  • B) 15.88"
  • C) 7.94"
  • D) 2.65"
Find vertical scale: \(\dfrac{1}{60}\rightarrow\dfrac{1"}{60"}\times\dfrac{12"}{1'} = 1":5'\) Find horizontal scale: \(vertical\ exaggeration: \dfrac{6}{1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1"}{5'}}{\dfrac{1"}{x'}} = \dfrac{x}{5}\) \(x = 30\rightarrow horizontal\ scale = 1":30'\) Plan horizontal distance: \(distance = \dfrac{79.4}{30} = 2.65"\)

Answer: D
Q48. What is the approximate elevation of the crest on section B-B'?
topo
  • A) 177'
  • B) 167'
  • C) 175'
  • D) 37'
Using the contours, we can find the elevation of the base of the trapezoid considering section B-B' is directly on the contour line \(130'+10' = 140' = Elevation\ at\ the\ base\ of\ trapezoid\) Find the height of the trapezoid in section B-B'. Crest is the top of the triangle. \(3y+30+4y = 290'\) \(y = 37.14\) \(140+37.14 = 177'\)

Answer: A
Q49. A new aerial photography project is to target the area shown in the illustration. The project will use the following parameters. Using the project parameter for end lap, what will be the forward advanced for each photograph?
photo
Porter Ranch Photogrammetry Project
Photo Scale:1 :12,000
Format:9 inch x 9 inch
End Lap:60%
Side Lap:30%
Camera Focal Length:6 inches
  • A) 3,600 ft
  • B) 4,450 ft
  • C) 5,110 ft
  • D) 3,350 ft
Find ground length: \(Ground\ length = (Format\ Size)\times\dfrac{1}{Photo\ Scale}\) \(Ground\ length = 9\ in\times\dfrac{12,000}{1}\times\dfrac{1\ ft}{12\ in}\) \(Ground\ length = 9,000\ ft\) The forward advance for each photograph is determined as follows: \(FWD_{ADV} = (Ground\ length)\times(1-End\ lap)\) \(= (9,000\ ft)\times(1-0.60)\) \(= 3,600\ ft\)

Answer: A
Q50. A 50' x 50' area of land is to be graded for a future proposed development. The existing contours are shown with the proposed rough grade elevations. What is the approximate volume of cut/fill for the net area?
area
  • A) 3700 CY cut
  • B) 1000 CY cut
  • C) 1800 CY cut
  • D) 2800 CY cut
For question like this, you need to split up the area into a grid and approximate the difference in the contour line and the proposed elevation for each grid box. Then multiply by the unit area. The sum of all the unit squares is the approximate volume. Draw a quick sketch. Select a height that is representative for the entire row of the area. Use averages of two contours if most of the unit area is between two contours. Total elevation difference for each row: first row \(((70-40)+(70-40)+(75-40)+(85-40)+(90-40)) = 190\ second\ row\) \(((60-45)+(60-45)+(65-45)+(75-45)+(85-45)) = 120\ third\ row\) \(((50-50)+(55-50)+(60-50)+(70-50)+(75-50)) = 60\ fourth\ row\) \(((40-45)+(45-45)+(55-45)+(65-45)+(75-45)) = 55\ fifth\ row\) \(((30-40)+(40-40)+(50-40)+(60-40)+(70-40)) = 50\ Total\ elevation\ difference\) for all squares times unit area: \((190+120+60+55+50)\times100ft^2 = 47500\ ft^3 = 1760\ CY\ cut\) Alternate Solution: The last method is very tedious problem and is subjective to how you interpret the grid. A simpler way is to find the average of the contours and the average of the land. Average contour is about 65. Average land height is about 45. \((65-45)\times50\times50 = 50,000\ ft^3 = 1850\ CY\ cut\) Considering the subjectivity of the question, the answer choices should be far enough apart that a unique answer can be chosen.

Answer: C
Q51. Which one of the followings are the advantages of LiDAR for data collection over most other techniques?
lidar
  • A) Higher resolutions
  • B) All of these
  • C) Centimeter accuracies
  • D) Ground detection in forested terrain
All of these are advantages of LiDAR over other surveying techniques.

Answer: B
Q52. Topographic maps differ from planimetric maps in that topographic maps:
topo
  • A) Contains only x-y coordinates
  • B) Can show natural and artificial features
  • C) Displays reliefs differently
  • D) Shows points on the vertical plane
Planimetric maps are maps which show only horizontal features and can only be seen on the ground from an aerial perspective also know as the "Plan" view. Examples include building footprints, road edges and curblines, sidewalks, trees, rivers, lakes, and utility poles. However anything the requires an elevation, has a z-coordinate, or on the veritcal plane all revolve around elevations which are not shown on a planimetric map and shown on a topographic map. A topographic map usually shows the same features as a planimetric map but uses contours or comparable symbols to show mountains, valleys, and plans, and, in the case of hydrographic charts, symbols and numbers to show depths in bodies of water.

Answer: D
Q53. What effect would neglecting curvature have on a rod reading?
level
  • A) Effect depends on instrument
  • B) Causes greater readings
  • C) Effect depends on weather
  • D) Causes smaller readings
Typically a rod reading will not require a curvature correction considering the sight distance through the level is not far. However an insignificant error will exist which will result in a greater rod reading since a horizontal line of sight does not bend with the curvature of the earth therefore the sight would be higher on a rod than intended.

Answer: B
Q54. An area of a map with a scale of 1 inch: 490 ft, as measured by a planimeter, is 3.78 in2. The ground area is
area
  • A) 8.91 acres
  • B) 0.04 acres
  • C) 20.84 acres
  • D) 5.51 acres
\(1\ in : 490\ ft\) \(1\ in^2 : (490\times490)\ ft^2\) \(1\ in^2 : 240100\ ft^2\) \(\dfrac{240100\times3.78}{43560\ ft^2/acres} = 20.84\ acres\)

Answer: C
Q55. What is the length of a horizontal curve with a long chord bearing of N73°14'E and bearing from EC to radius point of S29°13'W? The radius is 750'.
hc
  • A) 601.92'
  • B) 1015.13'
  • C) 1152.35'
  • D) 1203.84'
The line from the radius point to EC and BC always creates a 90 degree angle with the tangent line. \(Angle\ x = S73^\circ14'W-S29^\circ13'W = 44^\circ1'\) \(I = 91^\circ58'\) \(L = \dfrac{2\pi RI}{360} = \dfrac{2\pi(750)(91^\circ58')}{360}\) \(L = 1203.84'\)

Answer: D
